# containerkit

> Emit containerkit instead of a Compose file, a Dockerfile, and a shell script that drift apart. One program is the Engine SDK and the Compose SDK, in Go and in TSX.

Emit containerkit instead. The configuration and the operations are one program: the same names in Go and in TSX for a service, a volume, a network, a secret, a build, an image, a Swarm object, and a `pull`. The components and session methods are generated from the kit against pinned Moby and Compose SDKs, so configuration follows typed mappings rather than guessed YAML keys. `exportYAML` on a named `Compose` and `exportDockerfile` on a `Dockerfile` return the file text without dialing the daemon and without stopping a session. A live `docker.ts`, `docker.tsx`, or `docker.js` default-exports `root()` from `containerkit/live` and keeps the session open. `AsService` copies a container spec onto a Compose service, and `Validate` reports unsupported mappings. A Dockerfile is its own tree in `containerkit/dockerfile`: `<Run>` joins a layer, `<RunLayer>` starts the next, and `StopSignal` takes a POSIX name such as `SIGTERM`. Named constants (`proto`, `restartPolicy`, and the rest) come from `containerkit/vocab`. A closed vocabulary is that union. `pullPolicy`, `networkMode`, `ipc`, and `pid` also accept the prefix the helpers return. `mode` and `driver` stay strings.

```tsx
import { Compose, Service, Publish, exportYAML } from "containerkit";
import { proto } from "containerkit/vocab";

export default function App() {
  return (
    <Compose name="app">
      <Service
        name="api"
        image="alpine:latest"
        command={["sh", "-c", "mkdir -p /www && echo ok > /www/index.html && exec httpd -f -p 80 -h /www"]}
      >
        <Publish hostPort={8080} containerPort={80} protocol={proto.TCP} />
      </Service>
    </Compose>
  );
}

export const yaml = exportYAML(<App />);
```

Emit that module when the task is the file text. `exportYAML` returns the Compose text and accepts a named `Compose` only. `httpd` serves `/www/index.html`, which the command creates, and publishes `8080` to `80`. `false` disappears from the tree. `.map()` repeats a child. A function that returns a node is a component.

For a process that stays up, default-export `root()`. `fromEnv: true` uses the Docker host this machine's `docker` command already uses. A second `root()` throws while the first session is open. The session needs the `containerkit` binary on `PATH`, or `CONTAINERKIT_BIN`.

A function with no parameters renders again when state changes. Return a `Compose`, `Service`, `Job`, or `Container` and that tree is applied with a detached compose up. Return `null` and nothing is applied. The same YAML as last time applies nothing. `useSession()`, `useState()`, `useMemo()`, `useEffect()`, and `useResource()` belong to this function and throw outside it. `useMemo` returns `undefined` until a promise settles, then renders again. It writes the result under `.containerkit/memo` and skips the call when the same inputs come back.

```tsx
import { Compose, Service, Publish } from "containerkit";
import { proto } from "containerkit/vocab";
import { root, useMemo, useSession } from "containerkit/live";

export default root({ fromEnv: true, onExit: "down" }, function App() {
  const app = useSession();
  const ready = useMemo(() => app.pullImage("alpine:latest"), ["alpine:latest"]);
  if (!ready) return null;
  return (
    <Compose name="app">
      <Service
        name="api"
        image="alpine:latest"
        command={["sh", "-c", "mkdir -p /www && echo ok > /www/index.html && exec httpd -f -p 80 -h /www"]}
      >
        <Publish hostPort={8080} containerPort={80} protocol={proto.TCP} />
      </Service>
    </Compose>
  );
});
```

An `async` function, or a function that takes the session, runs once. It does not render again, and it does not call `useSession()`. Await the commands, then return the tree. A throw exits the process when this file is the program.

```tsx
import { Compose, Service } from "containerkit";
import { root } from "containerkit/live";

export default root({ fromEnv: true, onExit: "down" }, async function App(session) {
  await session.pullImage("alpine:latest");
  return (
    <Compose name="app">
      <Service name="api" image="alpine:latest" />
    </Compose>
  );
});
```

`onExit: "down"` takes the last applied project down on SIGINT and SIGTERM, then closes the session. Omit it and the containers stay up. `close()` closes the session and leaves the project running. `onUp` runs after a successful apply. `wait: true` waits until containers are running, and healthy when a service has a healthcheck, before `onUp`.

A successful `pullImage`, `pushImage`, `buildImage`, or `composeBuild` is `{ ok: true }`, and the TypeScript type stays `unknown`. `logs`, `attachContainer`, `statsContainer`, `copyFrom`, and `saveImages` stay untyped because they return a stream or a hijacked connection. `login`, `diskUsage`, `removeImage`, and the config, secret, plugin, node, service, task, checkpoint, and swarm lists and inspects return typed JSON. A nil list is `null`.

Pins verified 2026-11-12: `github.com/moby/moby/api` v1.56.1, `github.com/moby/moby/client` v0.6.2, `github.com/compose-spec/compose-go/v2` v2.16.2, `github.com/docker/compose/v5` v5.6.1.

## Docs

- [README](README.md): The project as components, the live session, the same names in Go, and how regeneration tracks the pinned SDKs. “A container becomes a service” is where `Validate` names each unsupported mapping.
- [TSX docs](tsx/docs/README.md): Reading order for a TypeScript user. Trees, the live session, the client, commands, then Dockerfiles.
- [Trees](tsx/docs/trees.md): Writing the project as components and exporting YAML from a named Compose node.
- [Live session](tsx/docs/live.md): `docker.ts`, `docker.tsx`, or `docker.js`, the render callback, the once callback, and `onExit: "down"`.
- [Commands](tsx/docs/commands.md): Session methods for images, containers, networks, volumes, Swarm, and Compose, including which results are typed.
- [Dockerfiles](tsx/docs/dockerfile.md): The Dockerfile tree, `Run` and `RunLayer`, and `exportDockerfile`.
- [Client](tsx/docs/client.md): Which daemon the session talks to. `connect` records settings and does not dial by itself.

## Examples

- [Live session](tsx/examples/docker.tsx): A `docker.tsx` that runs once, builds a small image, and stays open. `npm run live` from `tsx/` serves `http://127.0.0.1:18080`, and `onExit: "down"` takes the project down on Ctrl+C.
- [Supabase in TSX](tsx/examples/supabase.tsx): A full Compose project — gateway, Postgres, pooler, storage, logs — printed as YAML on stdout.
- [Image](tsx/examples/image.tsx): A multi-stage Dockerfile whose stages and layers follow the environment, printed on stdout.
- [Taskflow in TSX](tsx/examples/taskflow.tsx): A release graph. The image build overlaps Postgres. Lint waits for that image, then overlaps the database. Migrate retries. A failed check skips the tag. Down waits only for migrate, because unit and lint do not use Postgres, and still runs when migrate fails. Stdout is the plan document.
- [Supabase in Go](examples/supabase): The same stack written with the Go kit.
